finding_dispositions.evidence: Fresh r4 evidence replay and targeted conformance tests passed for no-follow initialization, fanout, and post-initialization objects/staging/locks/resources replacement. Descriptor-bound operations reject replaced attested ancestors before external mutation, and the independently rerun staging/final replacement probes did not mutate external targets.

The fresh r4 clock regression passed: expiry observation persists repository-owned high-water state, and later wall-clock rollback cannot revive the expired lease. Authoritative clock decisions remain transactionally bound to persistent high-water updates.

Fresh canonical-order and opposing-process tests passed. Cross-token resource acquisition validates the global canonical sequence before acquiring another resource, and opposing two-process requests terminate without deadlock.

The fresh exact claim/reconciliation regression passed. Direct CommitBatch validation binds the exact ordered lease-resource set, fence tokens, task lease, and same-transaction event payload, including missing, extra, empty, stale, and wrong-lease rejection.

Fresh connection tests passed for doctor and backup read-only enforcement. Read-only URI, query_only, and deny-by-default authorizer reject direct writes and WITH-prefixed UPDATE, DELETE, and INSERT statements.

Fresh replay/recovery corruption tests passed. Event index, transaction revision, transaction head, and task/head corruption are validated against authoritative replay and fail with repository integrity errors.

Independent separate-thread probes at object.after_staging_directory_fsync and object.after_publication now both raised ObjectIntegrityError, removed wrong staging/final names, left no available metadata, and retained no tampered bytes. The retained staging descriptor, staging name-to-inode check, final no-follow descriptor, expected-inode check, and repeated digest/name binding close the r3 available-wrong-bytes exploit.

In three independent repetitions, a separate thread replaced the final name with tampered bytes at object.after_object_directory_fsync, after the initial final descriptor verification and immediately before the mandated pre-transaction binding check. put_verified raised ObjectIntegrityError and left no metadata and no staging entry, but the canonical digest path still existed with the tampered bytes. Static inspection shows cleanup_final is set on initial final-open failure and post-commit verification failure, but not when the pre-transaction or in-transaction _verify_descriptor_binding raises.

findings.summary: A detected pre-transaction final-name replacement leaves the wrong file at the canonical digest path instead of safely clearing it.
findings.evidence: Using object.after_object_directory_fsync only as a synchronization barrier, a separate thread unlinked the published final and recreated it with different owner-approved-mode bytes. The next _verify_descriptor_binding correctly rejected the name-to-inode mismatch, but cleanup_final remained false. Across three runs the call failed and metadata stayed absent, while the tampered canonical final remained and staging was empty. This violates the governing Test Plan requirement that detected wrong final and staging names be cleared across the publication-to-metadata window.
findings.required_fix: Ensure every final binding mismatch after publication, including the pre-transaction and transaction-internal verification paths, schedules safe cleanup of the currently wrong final without deleting a concurrently installed verified inode. Preserve the retained descriptor/inode checks and quarantine any already committed metadata. Add a gate-bound separate-thread regression at object.after_object_directory_fsync, plus an equivalent transaction-window case, asserting call failure, empty staging, absent available metadata, and no tampered canonical final; retain dedup and fault-recovery regressions.
